model_note.S:
cc: Severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the back

HPI: 28 yo f. Patient reports: It started 12 hours ago. It is in the upper middle abdomen. It goes through to the mid-back. It is a deep, severe constant pain. It is 9/10. It has worsened and has not let up. It started after dinner; I had several alcoholic drinks over the weekend. Leaning forward helps slightly. Eating and lying flat worsen it. An antacid did not help. I had no previous episode this severe. I feel very nauseated. I have vomited 4 times and cannot keep water down. I feel weak. My heart feels fast with the pain.

Patient perspective: Are you going to judge me because I drink?

PMH: High triglycerides diagnosed 2 years ago; no known gallstones.

PSH: No abdominal surgeries.

Meds: Fenofibrate 145 mg daily, often missed.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Quit tobacco 2 years ago after 3 pack-years. Usually 3 beers nightly; 6 drinks at a gathering 2 days ago. No recreational drugs. Restaurant manager; lives with husband.

FH: Mother has diabetes; father has hyperlipidemia; sister healthy.

ROS: Gastrointestinal - Reports nausea. Reports vomiting. Denies melena. General - Denies fever. Reports fatigue. Denies weight loss. Cardiovascular - Denies chest pain. Reports palpitations. Denies syncope.
Reproductive history: I do not think I am pregnant, but I have not taken a pregnancy test.
Reproductive history: My last period was 2 weeks ago.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 99.4 F oral, P 112 bpm, BP 110/72 mmHg, R 22 rpm, Pulse Ox 97% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Leaning forward, visibly distressed by pain.

Heart: Regular tachycardia without murmur.

Lungs: Breath sounds present bilaterally without focal crackles.

Abd: On inspection, mild upper abdominal distention. Bowel sounds reduced in the examined quadrants. Marked epigastric tenderness. No involuntary guarding during gentle assessment. Tympany over the abdomen.

Osteopathic: T5 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Transfer to the emergency department now for severe persistent pain and inability to drink; obtain lipase, CBC, BMP, liver tests and triglycerides and assess biliary cause with ultrasound; provide monitored fluids and analgesia through the clinical team; explain concern for pancreatic inflammation and reassess organ function and disposition urgently.

2. Obtain ECG and appropriate cardiac biomarkers while evaluating upper abdominal pain; assess ischemic risk and hemodynamics; explain why the heart is considered even without classic chest pressure. Arrange urgent emergency-department or cardiology assessment if the history, ECG or biomarkers raise concern for an acute coronary syndrome.

3. Assess alcohol use nonjudgmentally and check bleeding symptoms; discuss reducing alcohol with appropriate withdrawal-risk assessment and acid treatment only after urgent causes are assessed; arrange follow-up support.

model_note.S:
cc: Severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the back

HPI: 28 yo f. Patient reports: It started 6 hours ago. It is in the upper middle abdomen. It goes through to the mid-back. It is a deep, severe constant pain. It is 9/10. It has worsened and has not let up. It started after dinner; I had several alcoholic drinks over the weekend. Leaning forward helps slightly. Eating and lying flat worsen it. An antacid did not help. I had no previous episode this severe. I feel very nauseated. I have vomited 4 times and cannot keep water down. I feel weak. My heart feels fast with the pain.

Patient perspective: Are you going to judge me because I drink?

PMH: High triglycerides diagnosed 2 years ago; no known gallstones.

PSH: No abdominal surgeries.

Meds: Fenofibrate 145 mg daily, often missed.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Quit tobacco 2 years ago after 3 pack-years. Usually 3 beers nightly; 6 drinks at a gathering 2 days ago. No recreational drugs. Restaurant manager; lives with husband.

FH: Mother has diabetes; father has hyperlipidemia; sister healthy.

ROS: Gastrointestinal - Reports nausea. Reports vomiting. Denies melena. General - Denies fever. Reports fatigue. Denies weight loss. Cardiovascular - Denies chest pain. Reports palpitations. Denies syncope.
Reproductive history: I do not think I am pregnant, but I have not taken a pregnancy test.
Reproductive history: My last period was 2 weeks ago.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 99.4 F oral, P 112 bpm, BP 110/72 mmHg, R 22 rpm, Pulse Ox 97% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Leaning forward, visibly distressed by pain.

Heart: Regular tachycardia without murmur.

Lungs: Breath sounds present bilaterally without focal crackles.

Abd: On inspection, mild upper abdominal distention. Bowel sounds reduced in the examined quadrants. Marked epigastric tenderness. No involuntary guarding during gentle assessment. Tympany over the abdomen.

Osteopathic: T5 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Transfer to the emergency department now for severe persistent pain and inability to drink; obtain lipase, CBC, BMP, liver tests and triglycerides and assess biliary cause with ultrasound; provide monitored fluids and analgesia through the clinical team; explain concern for pancreatic inflammation and reassess organ function and disposition urgently.

2. Obtain ECG and appropriate cardiac biomarkers while evaluating upper abdominal pain; assess ischemic risk and hemodynamics; explain why the heart is considered even without classic chest pressure. Arrange urgent emergency-department or cardiology assessment if the history, ECG or biomarkers raise concern for an acute coronary syndrome.

3. Assess alcohol use nonjudgmentally and check bleeding symptoms; discuss reducing alcohol with appropriate withdrawal-risk assessment and acid treatment only after urgent causes are assessed; arrange follow-up support.
